Research

Consumer behaviour in digital markets

What happens between hearing about a service and deciding to contact the seller? My MSc project with a wedding décor business in Wales first brought that question into focus for me. My wider interests include the information, people and digital tools that shape that decision.

Completed MSc research

Imani Events marketing plan

Cardiff Metropolitan University · Report dated January 2023

The research problem

Imani Events needed to decide where to focus its online marketing. For my 17,500-word MSc marketing plan, I asked how people first heard of the business, what they looked for in a wedding décor supplier and which digital services interested them.

Designing the questionnaire

I used Qualtrics to ask a single-choice question about discovery, rating questions about supplier choice, and a yes-or-no question about a planning app. These formats let me distinguish how people had found Imani Events from what they said they might use.

Who took part

The study plan proposed a convenience sample, with invitations by email and social media. The questionnaire returned 56 responses from Cardiff and elsewhere in Wales. The results do not identify which invitation channel brought in each respondent.

Reading the responses

I counted answers separately for each question. For importance ratings, I combined “very important” and “extremely important” and used the number who answered that item. I also reviewed competitors’ websites and search visibility to see where the survey findings could inform practical changes.

Primary research

Explore the survey findings

From finding a supplier to making an enquiry

Word of mouth was the most common way respondents had heard about Imani Events (31 of 54). When asked about choosing a supplier, 38 of 52 rated customer reviews and testimonials very or extremely important. This suggested that a website could help someone check a personal recommendation. I recommended showing photographs of past work alongside customer comments and making it easy to send an enquiry.

What the survey can tell us

The answers capture reported preferences around one business. People reached through the proposed recruitment channels may differ from other customers in Wales. The survey did not track bookings or link individual referrals to subsequent enquiries. For example, 36 of 49 respondents expressed interest in an app. Actual uptake would need a separate study.

A question for a follow-up study

After a personal referral, what does a couple still need to see before contacting a supplier? Interviews with people who enquired and people who decided against it could reveal what each group looked for and where they hesitated.

Prospective doctoral interests

Questions I would like to pursue

Digital Consumer Behaviour

When people choose an unfamiliar service online, what information prompts them to keep looking or to make an enquiry?

Artificial Intelligence in Marketing

How does explaining why an AI system recommended a product affect the way a shopper considers it?

Consumer Trust and Digital Decision-Making

When reviews disagree, how do buyers weigh other customers’ accounts against the seller’s response?

Social Commerce

How do shoppers weigh a friend’s suggestion against a creator’s recommendation when both appear in their feed?

Digital Customer Experience

When customers can try out a design on a website, what do they still want to discuss with the business before booking?
